title: "Inferential Tests"
format: html

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom)
source(here::here("scripts", "functions.R"))
```

## Hypotheses and analysis plan

Overall hypothesis: trust, acceptance and satisfaction are **lower when
participants were not asked for consent** (condition B) than when they were
asked (condition A).

| | Question | Analysis |
|---|---|---|
| H1a | Between-person effect of condition, separately for each vignette | Welch t-test per vignette × outcome (Wilcoxon rank-sum as a check) |
| H1b | Within-person effect of condition (A vs. B across a participant's three vignettes) | Linear mixed model with condition split into within- and between-person parts, vignette as a fixed effect, random intercept per participant |
| H1b follow-up | Does the condition effect differ across vignettes? | H1b model plus a condition × vignette interaction |
| H1b follow-up | Are the within-person effects negligible? | Equivalence tests (TOST) on the H1b estimates |
| H1b follow-up | Does the previous vignette's condition carry over? | H1b model on V2–V3 with the previous vignette's condition added |
| H2 | Do trust and acceptance predict satisfaction? | Linear mixed model with trust and acceptance split into within- and between-person parts |
| Exploratory | Among Asked vignettes, do ratings differ by consent decision? | Mixed model with consent decision (consented to both / mixed / declined both), plus a check of the same participants' Not asked ratings |
| Exploratory | Is the decision gap larger in Asked than Not asked vignettes? | Mixed model with participant consent rate × condition |
| Exploratory | Is Not asked closer to consenters than to decliners? | Absolute-gap contrast at the group level (cluster-robust SEs) and relative to each participant's own Not asked baseline |
| Exploratory | Is the own-baseline decline effect concentrated in V3? | Own-baseline model with decision × vignette; refits without V3, without participants whose decision changed, and without the random intercept |

Conventions:

- Condition effects are coded as **Not asked − Asked**, so a negative estimate
  is in the hypothesised direction.
- Tests are two-sided at α = .05. The hypothesis is directional, but two-sided
  tests are more conservative; for an estimate in the predicted direction the
  one-sided p is half the two-sided p.
- Holm correction is applied within each family of tests (the 9 H1a tests;
  the 3 H1b tests; the 3 interaction tests). The follow-up analyses are
  secondary checks on H1b and are interpreted descriptively.
- Satisfaction is a single 1–5 item, so H1b and H2 are repeated with
  cumulative link mixed models (ordinal regression) as a sensitivity check.

## Load data

The same panel as `descriptives.qmd`: participants who answered at least one
vignette. Data are reshaped to one row per participant per vignette.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

panel <- read_csv(here::here("data", "data_clean.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(if_any(matches("^v[1-3]_status1$"), \(x) !is.na(x)))

outcomes <- panel |>
  pivot_vignettes_long() |>
  mutate(
    vignette = factor(vignette, labels = paste0("V", 1:3)),
    condition = factor(
      if_else(status1 == "Was not asked for consent", "Not asked", "Asked"),
      levels = c("Asked", "Not asked")
    )
  ) |>
  select(ResponseId, vignette, condition, trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction)

outcome_labels <- c(
  trust_score = "Trust",
  accept_score = "Acceptance",
  satisfaction = "Satisfaction"
)

outcomes |>
  count(vignette, condition) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n)

outcomes |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x))))
```

## H1a: Between-person effect of condition, by vignette

Within each vignette, different participants were in the Asked and Not asked
conditions, so these are independent-groups comparisons. Welch's t-test is
used because it does not assume equal variances. The outcomes are bounded 1–5
scores; with about 29 per group the t-test is reasonably robust to their
non-normality, and the Wilcoxon rank-sum test is reported as a check
(particularly for satisfaction, a single ordinal item).

Effect sizes are Hedges' g (Not asked − Asked, using an unpooled SD to match
Welch).

```{r}
#| label: h1a

h1a <- outcomes |>
  # Put "Not asked" first so estimates are Not asked − Asked
  mutate(condition = fct_relevel(condition, "Not asked")) |>
  pivot_longer(names(outcome_labels), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(outcome_labels[measure], levels = outcome_labels)) |>
  nest(.by = c(measure, vignette)) |>
  mutate(
    welch = map(data, \(d) tidy(t.test(value ~ condition, data = d))),
    g = map(data, \(d) {
      effectsize::hedges_g(value ~ condition, data = d, pooled_sd = FALSE) |>
        as_tibble()
    }),
    wilcox_p = map_dbl(data, \(d) {
      wilcox.test(value ~ condition, data = d, exact = FALSE)$p.value
    })
  ) |>
  select(-data) |>
  unnest(welch) |>
  unnest(g, names_sep = "_") |>
  transmute(
    measure, vignette,
    diff = estimate, conf_low = conf.low, conf_high = conf.high,
    t = statistic, df = parameter, p = p.value,
    g = g_Hedges_g, g_low = g_CI_low, g_high = g_CI_high,
    wilcox_p
  ) |>
  mutate(
    p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"),
    wilcox_p_holm = p.adjust(wilcox_p, "holm")
  )

h1a |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-h1a
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(h1a, aes(x = diff, y = fct_rev(vignette), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure)) +
  labs(
    x = "Not asked − Asked (scale points, 95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Negative values are in the hypothesised direction"
  )
```

How large a difference could these comparisons reliably detect? With about 29
per group, a two-sided t-test at α = .05 has 80% power only for a
standardised difference of:

```{r}
#| label: h1a-power

power.t.test(n = 29, power = 0.8, sd = 1, sig.level = 0.05)$delta
```

## H1b: Within-person effect of condition

Every participant saw both conditions (two vignettes in one, one in the
other). The condition indicator (`not_asked` = 1 for Not asked) is split into:

- `not_asked_w`: the participant's deviation from their own mean, i.e. the
  **within-person** effect of being in the Not asked condition for a given
  vignette compared with that participant's other vignettes.
- `not_asked_pm`: the participant's proportion of Not asked vignettes (1/3 or
  2/3). This between-person part is confounded with the condition order and is
  included only so that `not_asked_w` is a pure within-person estimate.

Vignette is a fixed effect, so differences between vignettes (which also
reflect their presentation order) are not attributed to condition. With three
observations per participant, only a random intercept is estimated.

```{r}
#| label: h1b

mm_data <- outcomes |>
  mutate(
    not_asked = as.integer(condition == "Not asked"),
    not_asked_pm = mean(not_asked),
    .by = ResponseId
  ) |>
  mutate(not_asked_w = not_asked - not_asked_pm)

fit_cond <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(c("not_asked_w", "not_asked_pm", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y),
    data = mm_data
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

h1b_all <- imap(fit_cond, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

h1b <- h1b_all |>
  filter(term == "not_asked_w") |>
  mutate(
    p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, "holm"),
    # Approximate standardised effect: estimate / total SD of the outcome
    d = estimate / map_dbl(names(outcome_labels), \(y) sd(mm_data[[y]]))
  ) |>
  select(measure, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, statistic,
         p.value, p_holm, d)

h1b |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Full fixed effects, for reference:

```{r}
#| label: h1b-full

h1b_all |>
  select(measure, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Random-effect variances and singular-fit check:

```{r}
#| label: h1b-varcorr

imap(fit_cond, \(m, nm) {
  as_tibble(VarCorr(m)) |>
    transmute(measure = nm, component = grp, variance = round(vcov, 3)) |>
    mutate(singular = isSingular(m))
}) |>
  list_rbind()
```

## H1b follow-ups

### Condition × vignette interaction

Does the effect of not being asked differ between vignettes? The H1b model is
extended with a `not_asked × vignette` interaction. `not_asked_pm` stays in the
model, so the condition effects remain adjusted for each participant's
proportion of Not asked vignettes. The interaction is tested with a
Satterthwaite F-test (2 df) for each outcome, Holm-corrected across the three
outcomes.

```{r}
#| label: interaction

fit_int <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(
      c("not_asked_pm", "not_asked * vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"),
      y
    ),
    data = mm_data
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

int_tests <- imap(fit_int, \(m, nm) {
  a <- anova(m)["not_asked:vignette", ]
  tibble(
    measure = nm,
    F = a[["F value"]],
    num_df = a[["NumDF"]],
    den_df = a[["DenDF"]],
    p = a[["Pr(>F)"]]
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"))

int_tests |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Condition effect (Not asked − Asked) within each vignette from the
interaction models, with unadjusted 95% CIs. These are shown to describe the
pattern; with 9 estimates, one or two nominally significant results would not
be surprising by chance.

```{r}
#| label: interaction-slopes

int_slopes <- imap(fit_int, \(m, nm) {
  emmeans::emtrends(m, ~ vignette, var = "not_asked", lmer.df = "satterthwaite") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  rename(
    estimate = not_asked.trend, std_error = SE,
    conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, t = t.ratio, p = p.value
  ) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels))

int_slopes |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-interaction
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(
  int_slopes,
  aes(x = estimate, y = fct_rev(vignette), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure)) +
  labs(
    x = "Not asked − Asked (scale points, 95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Negative values are in the hypothesised direction"
  )
```

These per-vignette estimates differ from the raw H1a differences because the
model also uses each participant's ratings of the other vignettes to adjust
for their overall level.

### Equivalence tests (TOST)

A non-significant result does not show that an effect is absent. Two one-sided
tests (TOST) check whether the within-person effect from H1b is smaller than
an equivalence bound ±Δ: equivalence is declared at α = .05 when the 90% CI
lies entirely inside (−Δ, Δ). The tests use the H1b estimates, standard
errors and Satterthwaite df.

No smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) was pre-specified, so two things are
reported:

1. The **smallest bound** at which each effect would be declared equivalent
   (the larger absolute end of the 90% CI), in scale points and SD units.
2. TOST p-values for several candidate bounds: ±0.25 and ±0.5 scale points
   (a quarter and half of one response option) and ±0.2 and ±0.5 SD (Cohen's
   small and medium).

The SESOI should ideally be chosen on substantive grounds before looking at
these results.

```{r}
#| label: tost

tost_p <- function(est, se, df, bound) {
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df)
  pmax(p_lower, p_upper)
}

h1b_tost <- h1b |>
  mutate(
    sd_y = map_dbl(names(outcome_labels), \(y) sd(mm_data[[y]])),
    ci90_low = estimate - qt(0.95, df) * std.error,
    ci90_high = estimate + qt(0.95, df) * std.error,
    min_bound = pmax(abs(ci90_low), abs(ci90_high)),
    min_bound_sd = min_bound / sd_y
  )

h1b_tost |>
  select(measure, estimate, ci90_low, ci90_high, min_bound, min_bound_sd) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

tost_bounds <- tibble(
  bound_label = c("±0.25 points", "±0.5 points", "±0.2 SD", "±0.5 SD"),
  in_sd = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE),
  value = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.2, 0.5)
)

tost_grid <- cross_join(h1b_tost, tost_bounds) |>
  mutate(
    bound = if_else(in_sd, value * sd_y, value),
    p_tost = tost_p(estimate, std.error, df, bound),
    equivalent = p_tost < 0.05
  ) |>
  select(measure, bound_label, bound, p_tost, equivalent)

tost_grid |>
  mutate(bound = round(bound, 3), p_tost = signif(p_tost, 3))
```

### Carryover from the previous vignette

Could being asked (or not) in one vignette affect ratings of the next? For V2
and V3, `prev_not_asked` is the condition of the preceding vignette (V1 has no
predecessor, so it is excluded). The H1b model is refitted on V2–V3 with the
current and previous condition. `not_asked_pm` (computed over all three
vignettes) is kept so the condition effects remain within-person.

```{r}
#| label: carryover

carry_data <- mm_data |>
  arrange(ResponseId, vignette) |>
  mutate(prev_not_asked = lag(not_asked), .by = ResponseId) |>
  filter(!is.na(prev_not_asked))

carry_data |>
  count(vignette, not_asked, prev_not_asked)

fit_carry <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(
      c("not_asked", "prev_not_asked", "not_asked_pm", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"),
      y
    ),
    data = carry_data
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

carryover <- imap(fit_carry, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(term %in% c("not_asked", "prev_not_asked"))

carryover |>
  select(measure, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Most participants switched condition between consecutive vignettes, so
`not_asked` and `prev_not_asked` are negatively correlated, which widens both
CIs:

```{r}
#| label: carryover-cor

cor(carry_data$not_asked, carry_data$prev_not_asked)
```

Does the effect of the current condition depend on the previous one (e.g. a
contrast effect when switching from Asked to Not asked)?

```{r}
#| label: carryover-interaction

imap(fit_carry, \(m, nm) {
  a <- anova(update(m, . ~ . + not_asked:prev_not_asked))["not_asked:prev_not_asked", ]
  tibble(measure = nm, F = a[["F value"]], den_df = a[["DenDF"]], p = a[["Pr(>F)"]])
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

## H2: Do trust and acceptance predict satisfaction?

Trust and acceptance are each split into a person mean (`*_pm`, the
**between-person** part: do people who are generally more trusting report
higher satisfaction?) and a deviation from that mean (`*_w`, the
**within-person** part: when a participant trusts MedHelper more in one
vignette than usual, are they also more satisfied?). Condition and vignette
are included as covariates.

Three models are fitted: trust alone, acceptance alone, and both together.
Trust and acceptance are strongly correlated (see `descriptives.qmd`), so the
joint model shows each one's unique contribution, and collinearity is checked.

These are associations between ratings given at the same time by the same
person; they do not establish that trust or acceptance causes satisfaction.

```{r}
#| label: h2

h2_data <- mm_data |>
  mutate(
    trust_pm = mean(trust_score),
    accept_pm = mean(accept_score),
    .by = ResponseId
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trust_w = trust_score - trust_pm,
    accept_w = accept_score - accept_pm
  )

fit_h2 <- list(
  `Trust only` = lmer(
    satisfaction ~ trust_w + trust_pm + not_asked + vignette + (1 | ResponseId),
    data = h2_data
  ),
  `Acceptance only` = lmer(
    satisfaction ~ accept_w + accept_pm + not_asked + vignette + (1 | ResponseId),
    data = h2_data
  ),
  `Both` = lmer(
    satisfaction ~ trust_w + trust_pm + accept_w + accept_pm + not_asked +
      vignette + (1 | ResponseId),
    data = h2_data
  )
)

h2 <- imap(fit_h2, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(model = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(model = fct_inorder(model))

h2 |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "trust|accept")) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

Estimates are in scale points: e.g. `accept_w` is the change in satisfaction
for a 1-point increase in acceptance relative to the participant's own
average.

Variance explained (Nakagawa's R²; marginal = fixed effects only,
conditional = including the participant random intercept):

```{r}
#| label: h2-r2

imap(fit_h2, \(m, nm) {
  r2 <- performance::r2_nakagawa(m)
  tibble(
    model = nm,
    r2_marginal = r2$R2_marginal,
    r2_conditional = r2$R2_conditional
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Collinearity in the joint model:

```{r}
#| label: h2-collinearity

performance::check_collinearity(fit_h2$Both)
```

## Exploratory: consent decision among Asked participants

This analysis was not part of the original hypotheses. In the Asked
condition, participants answered two consent requests per vignette. Their
decision is coded as:

- **Consented to both** (reference group)
- **Mixed**: consented to one request, declined the other
- **Declined both**

Participants chose their answers, so differences between these groups describe
who made which choice; they are not effects of consenting. A participant's
decision may itself reflect how much they already trusted MedHelper.

```{r}
#| label: decision-data

asked <- outcomes |>
  filter(condition == "Asked") |>
  left_join(
    panel |>
      pivot_vignettes_long() |>
      mutate(vignette = factor(vignette, labels = paste0("V", 1:3))) |>
      select(ResponseId, vignette, status1, status2),
    by = join_by(ResponseId, vignette)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_consent = (status1 == "Consented to MedHelper") +
      (status2 == "Consented to MedHelper"),
    decision = factor(
      n_consent,
      levels = 2:0,
      labels = c("Consented to both", "Mixed", "Declined both")
    )
  )

asked |>
  summarise(observations = n(), participants = n_distinct(ResponseId), .by = decision) |>
  arrange(decision)

# Participants with two Asked vignettes: did their decision change?
asked |>
  summarise(
    asked_vignettes = n(),
    distinct_decisions = n_distinct(decision),
    .by = ResponseId
  ) |>
  count(asked_vignettes, distinct_decisions)
```

Few participants made different decisions across their Asked vignettes, so the
comparison below is almost entirely between people.

### Ratings by consent decision

Linear mixed model per outcome on the Asked rows, with vignette as a fixed
effect and a random intercept per participant. The overall decision effect is
tested with a Satterthwaite F-test (Holm-corrected across outcomes); each
group is then compared with "Consented to both" (Holm-adjusted within outcome;
the CIs use the matching Bonferroni adjustment).

```{r}
#| label: decision-models

fit_dec <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("decision", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y), data = asked)
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

dec_omnibus <- imap(fit_dec, \(m, nm) {
  a <- anova(m)["decision", ]
  tibble(
    measure = nm,
    F = a[["F value"]],
    num_df = a[["NumDF"]],
    den_df = a[["DenDF"]],
    p = a[["Pr(>F)"]]
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"))

dec_omnibus |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

dec_contrasts <- imap(fit_dec, \(m, nm) {
  emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ decision, lmer.df = "satterthwaite") |>
    emmeans::contrast("trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, adjust = "holm") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  select(
    measure, contrast, estimate, std_error = SE, df,
    conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value
  ) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels))

dec_contrasts |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-decision
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(
  dec_contrasts,
  aes(x = estimate, y = fct_rev(contrast), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure)) +
  labs(x = "Difference from Consented to both (scale points, adjusted 95% CI)", y = NULL)
```

As a single-df alternative, the number of consents given (0, 1 or 2) as a
linear predictor:

```{r}
#| label: decision-trend

fit_dec_trend <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("n_consent", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y), data = asked)
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

imap(fit_dec_trend, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(term == "n_consent") |>
  select(measure, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

Ordinal check for satisfaction (log-odds scale; negative = lower
satisfaction than Consented to both):

```{r}
#| label: decision-ordinal

clmm_dec <- ordinal::clmm(
  factor(satisfaction, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE) ~ decision + vignette +
    (1 | ResponseId),
  data = asked,
  nAGQ = 10
)

coef(summary(clmm_dec)) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "term") |>
  filter(str_starts(term, "decision")) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

### Is the decision a marker of pre-existing attitudes?

If declining reflects a participant's general stance towards MedHelper, the
same participants should also give lower ratings in vignettes where they were
**not** asked, where no decision was made. Each participant's consent rate
(proportion of consent requests accepted across their Asked vignettes, 0–1) is
used to predict their Not asked ratings.

```{r}
#| label: decision-disposition

person_consent <- asked |>
  summarise(consent_rate = mean(n_consent) / 2, .by = ResponseId)

not_asked_rows <- outcomes |>
  filter(condition == "Not asked") |>
  inner_join(person_consent, by = join_by(ResponseId))

fit_disp <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(c("consent_rate", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y),
    data = not_asked_rows
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

disposition <- imap(fit_disp, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, singular = isSingular(m), .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(term == "consent_rate")

disposition |>
  select(measure, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value, singular) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

The estimate is the difference in Not asked ratings between a participant who
accepted every consent request and one who declined every request. A singular
fit means the participant random-intercept variance was estimated as zero
(many participants have only one Not asked vignette), so that model reduces to
ordinary regression with vignette as a covariate.

### Is the decision gap larger when participants were asked?

If the consent decision only marks a pre-existing stance, the gap between
high- and low-consenting participants should be about the same in their Asked
and Not asked vignettes. If being asked (and choosing) adds something, the gap
should be larger in the Asked vignettes.

This is tested with all vignettes in one model per outcome: the participant's
consent rate × condition (`asked` = 1 for Asked), with `not_asked_pm` and
vignette as covariates and a random intercept per participant. The
`consent_rate:asked` interaction is the difference between the two gaps
(Asked minus Not asked), in scale points for going from declining every
request to accepting every request. Because each participant contributes to
both conditions, this is largely a within-person comparison. Holm correction
is applied across the three outcomes.

The consent rate is the same person-level value in both conditions, so the
Asked gap here can differ slightly from the vignette-specific decision
contrasts above (10 participants made different decisions in their two Asked
vignettes).

```{r}
#| label: decision-gap

gap_data <- mm_data |>
  inner_join(person_consent, by = join_by(ResponseId)) |>
  mutate(asked = 1L - not_asked)

fit_gap <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(
      c("consent_rate * asked", "not_asked_pm", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"),
      y
    ),
    data = gap_data
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

gap_slopes <- imap(fit_gap, \(m, nm) {
  emmeans::emtrends(
    m, ~ asked, var = "consent_rate",
    at = list(asked = 0:1), lmer.df = "satterthwaite"
  ) |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  transmute(
    measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels),
    condition = if_else(asked == 1, "Asked", "Not asked"),
    gap = consent_rate.trend, conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value
  )

gap_slopes |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

gap_interaction <- imap(fit_gap, \(m, nm) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, singular = isSingular(m), .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(term == "consent_rate:asked") |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, "holm"))

gap_interaction |>
  select(measure, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, df, p.value, p_holm, singular) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-decision-gap
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3

ggplot(
  gap_slopes,
  aes(x = gap, y = fct_rev(condition), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure)) +
  labs(
    x = "Rating gap: accept all vs. decline all requests (scale points, 95% CI)",
    y = NULL
  )
```

Ordinal check for satisfaction (log-odds scale):

```{r}
#| label: decision-gap-ordinal

clmm_gap <- ordinal::clmm(
  factor(satisfaction, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE) ~
    consent_rate * asked + not_asked_pm + vignette + (1 | ResponseId),
  data = gap_data,
  nAGQ = 10
)

coef(summary(clmm_gap)) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "term") |>
  filter(term == "consent_rate:asked") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

### Is Not asked closer to consenters than to decliners?

This asks whether the gap between Not asked and "Declined both" ratings is
larger than the gap between Not asked and "Consented to both" ratings. The
two gaps share Not asked as their reference, so:

- With **signed** gaps, (Declined − Not asked) − (Consented − Not asked)
  reduces to Declined − Consented, which is tested above.
- With **absolute** gaps, and given Consented ≥ Not asked ≥ Declined (checked
  below), |Declined − Not asked| − |Consented − Not asked| =
  2 × Not asked − Consented − Declined. A positive value means Not asked
  ratings are closer to consenters than to decliners.

It is answered in two ways:

1. **Group level.** All 174 observations are classified by status (Not asked,
   Consented to both, Mixed, Declined both) and compared as groups. A linear
   model with vignette as a covariate is used, with cluster-robust (CR1)
   standard errors by participant and df = participants − 1. A random-intercept
   model is not used here because it would partly compare each person with
   their own other ratings, blending this question with the next one.
2. **Each participant's own baseline.** For each Asked observation, the
   outcome is re-expressed as the difference from the same participant's mean
   rating in their Not asked vignettes. These own-baseline gaps are compared
   across decisions with a mixed model (vignette fixed effect, random intercept
   per participant). Here, the "Consented gap" and "Declined gap" are the
   estimated mean gaps for those decisions.

Holm correction is applied across the three outcomes for each contrast.

```{r}
#| label: status-gap-group

status_data <- mm_data |>
  left_join(select(asked, ResponseId, vignette, decision), by = join_by(ResponseId, vignette)) |>
  mutate(
    status = if_else(condition == "Not asked", "Not asked", as.character(decision)),
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c("Not asked", "Consented to both", "Mixed", "Declined both")
    )
  )

status_data |>
  count(status)

n_clusters <- n_distinct(status_data$ResponseId)

# Contrast weights over (Not asked, Consented to both, Mixed, Declined both)
group_gap_contrasts <- list(
  `Consented − Not asked` = c(-1, 1, 0, 0),
  `Declined − Not asked` = c(-1, 0, 0, 1),
  `|Declined gap| − |Consented gap|` = c(2, -1, 0, -1)
)

status_group <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  m <- lm(reformulate(c("status", "vignette"), y), data = status_data)
  V <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = ~ ResponseId, type = "HC1")
  emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ status, vcov. = V, df = n_clusters - 1)
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

status_means <- imap(status_group, \(e, nm) {
  summary(e) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  transmute(
    measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels),
    status, mean = emmean, conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL
  )

status_means |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

# The absolute-gap contrast assumes Consented >= Not asked >= Declined
status_means |>
  select(measure, status, mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = mean) |>
  mutate(ordering_holds = `Consented to both` >= `Not asked` & `Not asked` >= `Declined both`) |>
  select(measure, ordering_holds)

gap_group <- imap(status_group, \(e, nm) {
  emmeans::contrast(e, group_gap_contrasts) |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, "holm"), .by = contrast) |>
  select(
    measure, contrast, estimate, std_error = SE, df,
    conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value, p_holm
  )

gap_group |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: status-gap-own

own_baseline <- outcomes |>
  filter(condition == "Not asked") |>
  summarise(
    across(names(outcome_labels), mean, .names = "{.col}_base"),
    .by = ResponseId
  )

own_gap_data <- asked |>
  inner_join(own_baseline, by = join_by(ResponseId)) |>
  mutate(
    trust_score = trust_score - trust_score_base,
    accept_score = accept_score - accept_score_base,
    satisfaction = satisfaction - satisfaction_base
  )

# Observed mean own-baseline gaps
own_gap_data |>
  pivot_longer(names(outcome_labels), names_to = "measure", values_to = "gap") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(outcome_labels[measure], levels = outcome_labels)) |>
  summarise(mean_gap = round(mean(gap), 2), n = n(), .by = c(measure, decision)) |>
  arrange(measure, decision)

fit_own_gap <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(reformulate(c("decision", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y), data = own_gap_data)
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

# Contrast weights over (Consented to both, Mixed, Declined both)
own_gap_contrasts <- list(
  `Consented gap` = c(1, 0, 0),
  `Declined gap` = c(0, 0, 1),
  `|Declined gap| − |Consented gap|` = c(-1, 0, -1),
  `Declined − Consented (signed)` = c(-1, 0, 1)
)

gap_own <- imap(fit_own_gap, \(m, nm) {
  emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ decision, lmer.df = "satterthwaite") |>
    emmeans::contrast(own_gap_contrasts) |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(measure = nm, singular = isSingular(m), .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, "holm"), .by = contrast) |>
  select(
    measure, contrast, estimate, std_error = SE, df,
    conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value, p_holm, singular
  )

gap_own |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

The absolute-gap contrast in the own-baseline model assumes the Consented gap
is positive and the Declined gap negative; check this in the table above
before interpreting it.

The two analyses address different questions. The group-level comparison
includes the fact that decliners are generally lower raters (see the
consent-rate analysis above). The own-baseline comparison removes each
person's general level, so it reflects how ratings in the vignette where a
decision was made differ from that person's own Not asked ratings. A
vignette-specific decision may still reflect a vignette-specific reaction
(e.g. disliking that particular scenario), so neither comparison isolates an
effect of the decision itself.

### Is the own-baseline decline effect concentrated in V3?

Most "Declined both" ratings come from V3, so the signed own-baseline
difference (Declined − Consented) may be driven by that vignette. This is
checked in three ways:

1. **Decision × vignette.** The own-baseline model is refitted with a
   decision × vignette interaction (Satterthwaite F-test, Holm-corrected
   across outcomes). Declined − Consented is then estimated within each
   vignette, and V3 is compared with the average of V1 and V2.
2. **Leaving out V3.** The original own-baseline model is refitted without
   the V3 "Declined both" ratings, and without V3 altogether.
3. **Who carries the estimate.** The random intercept absorbs each
   participant's general level, so the model leans on participants whose
   decision differed between their two Asked vignettes: for them, Declined −
   Consented is a direct within-person comparison. The model is refitted
   without these participants, and also without the random intercept
   (ordinary regression with cluster-robust CR1 SEs by participant), which
   weights every observation equally.

```{r}
#| label: own-gap-v3-counts

own_gap_data |>
  count(vignette, decision) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = decision, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Participants whose decision differed between their two Asked vignettes
switchers <- own_gap_data |>
  summarise(n_decisions = n_distinct(decision), .by = ResponseId) |>
  filter(n_decisions > 1) |>
  pull(ResponseId)

length(switchers)

# Switchers who declined both requests in one vignette: which vignette?
switcher_declines <- own_gap_data |>
  filter(ResponseId %in% switchers, decision == "Declined both") |>
  count(vignette, name = "participants")

switcher_declines
```

```{r}
#| label: own-gap-v3-interaction

fit_own_v <- map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
  lmer(
    reformulate(c("decision * vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y),
    data = own_gap_data
  )
}) |>
  set_names(outcome_labels)

own_v_int <- imap(fit_own_v, \(m, nm) {
  a <- anova(m)["decision:vignette", ]
  tibble(
    measure = nm,
    F = a[["F value"]],
    num_df = a[["NumDF"]],
    den_df = a[["DenDF"]],
    p = a[["Pr(>F)"]]
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"))

own_v_int |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

# Declined − Consented within each vignette, then V3 against V1–V2
own_v_dc <- imap(fit_own_v, \(m, nm) {
  dc <- emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ decision | vignette, lmer.df = "satterthwaite") |>
    emmeans::contrast(list(`Declined − Consented` = c(-1, 0, 1)))

  by_vignette <- summary(dc, infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(comparison = as.character(vignette), estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value)

  v3_vs_rest <- emmeans::contrast(
    dc,
    list(`V1–V2 average` = c(0.5, 0.5, 0), `V3 − V1–V2 average` = c(-0.5, -0.5, 1)),
    by = NULL
  ) |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(comparison = as.character(contrast), estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value)

  bind_rows(by_vignette, v3_vs_rest) |>
    mutate(measure = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  rename(std_error = SE, conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels))

own_v_dc |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: own-gap-v3-sensitivity

# Signed Declined − Consented own-baseline difference for a given data set
signed_dc <- function(data, mixed = TRUE) {
  data <- droplevels(data)

  map(names(outcome_labels), \(y) {
    if (mixed) {
      m <- lmer(reformulate(c("decision", "vignette", "(1 | ResponseId)"), y), data = data)
      e <- emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ decision, lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
    } else {
      m <- lm(reformulate(c("decision", "vignette"), y), data = data)
      V <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = ~ ResponseId, type = "HC1")
      e <- emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ decision, vcov. = V, df = n_distinct(data$ResponseId) - 1)
    }

    emmeans::contrast(e, list(`Declined − Consented` = c(-1, 0, 1))) |>
      summary(infer = TRUE) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(measure = outcome_labels[[y]], n_declined = sum(data$decision == "Declined both"))
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}

own_v_sens <- list(
  `All observations` = signed_dc(own_gap_data),
  `Without V3 Declined-both ratings` = signed_dc(
    filter(own_gap_data, !(vignette == "V3" & decision == "Declined both"))
  ),
  `Without V3` = signed_dc(filter(own_gap_data, vignette != "V3")),
  `Without decision switchers` = signed_dc(filter(own_gap_data, !ResponseId %in% switchers)),
  `No random intercept (CR1 SEs)` = signed_dc(own_gap_data, mixed = FALSE)
) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "fit") |>
  transmute(
    fit = fct_inorder(fit),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = outcome_labels),
    n_declined, estimate, std_error = SE, df,
    conf_low = lower.CL, conf_high = upper.CL, p = p.value
  ) |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"), .by = fit)

own_v_sens |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-own-gap-v3-sensitivity
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(
  own_v_sens,
  aes(x = estimate, y = fct_rev(fit), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure)) +
  labs(
    x = "Own-baseline Declined − Consented (scale points, 95% CI)",
    y = NULL
  )
```

The decision × vignette test has very little power: V1 and V2 contain only a
handful of "Declined both" ratings, so their vignette-specific estimates are
imprecise. The leave-out refits are therefore the more informative check.

## Assumption checks

Residuals from the linear mixed models. Satisfaction takes only five values,
so its residuals fall on parallel lines; this is expected and is the reason
for the ordinal sensitivity models below.

```{r}
#| label: residuals
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

model_residuals <- c(
  set_names(fit_cond, paste("H1b:", names(fit_cond))),
  set_names(fit_h2["Both"], "H2: Both")
) |>
  imap(\(m, nm) tibble(model = nm, fitted = fitted(m), resid = resid(m))) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(model = fct_inorder(model))

ggplot(model_residuals, aes(x = fitted, y = resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Fitted value", y = "Residual")

ggplot(model_residuals, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_qq_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(model)) +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantile", y = "Residual")
```

Normality of the participant random intercepts:

```{r}
#| label: ranef-qq
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5

c(fit_cond, set_names(fit_h2["Both"], "H2: Both")) |>
  imap(\(m, nm) tibble(model = nm, intercept = ranef(m)$ResponseId[[1]])) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(model = fct_inorder(model)) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = intercept)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.6) +
  stat_qq_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantile", y = "Random intercept")
```

### Influence of the largest H2 residual

The joint H2 model has one large negative residual. Refitting without that
observation checks whether it drives the results.

```{r}
#| label: h2-outlier

outlier <- which.max(abs(resid(fit_h2$Both)))

h2_data[outlier, ] |>
  select(ResponseId, vignette, condition, trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction)

bind_rows(
  `All observations` = h2 |> filter(model == "Both"),
  `Outlier removed` = update(fit_h2$Both, data = h2_data[-outlier, ]) |>
    broom.mixed::tidy(effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE),
  .id = "fit"
) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "trust|accept")) |>
  select(fit, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  arrange(term, fit) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

### Ordinal sensitivity models for satisfaction

Cumulative link mixed models (`ordinal::clmm`, logit link) treat satisfaction
as ordered categories rather than an interval score. Estimates are on the
log-odds scale, so only their direction and p-values are comparable with the
linear models.

```{r}
#| label: ordinal

table(satisfaction = h2_data$satisfaction)

ord_data <- h2_data |>
  mutate(sat_ord = factor(satisfaction, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE))

clmm_cond <- ordinal::clmm(
  sat_ord ~ not_asked_w + not_asked_pm + vignette + (1 | ResponseId),
  data = ord_data,
  nAGQ = 10
)

clmm_h2 <- ordinal::clmm(
  sat_ord ~ trust_w + trust_pm + accept_w + accept_pm + not_asked + vignette +
    (1 | ResponseId),
  data = ord_data,
  nAGQ = 10
)

ordinal_terms <- c("not_asked_w", "trust_w", "trust_pm", "accept_w", "accept_pm")

list(`H1b: Satisfaction` = clmm_cond, `H2: Both` = clmm_h2) |>
  imap(\(m, nm) {
    coef(summary(m)) |>
      as_tibble(rownames = "term") |>
      filter(term %in% ordinal_terms) |>
      mutate(model = nm, .before = 1)
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  rename(estimate = Estimate, std_error = `Std. Error`, z = `z value`, p = `Pr(>|z|)`) |>
  mutate(
    odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
    across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-values
#| include: false

f2 <- \(x) format(round(x, 2), nsmall = 2)
fp <- \(p) if_else(p < .001, "< .001", paste("=", format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3)))

h1a_neg <- sum(h1a$diff < 0)
h1a_min_p <- min(h1a$p)
power_d <- power.t.test(n = 29, power = 0.8, sd = 1, sig.level = 0.05)$delta

h1b_row <- \(m) filter(h1b, measure == m)
h1b_text <- \(m) {
  r <- h1b_row(m)
  glue::glue(
    "{str_to_lower(m)} b = {f2(r$estimate)} [{f2(r$conf.low)}, {f2(r$conf.high)}], p {fp(r$p.value)}"
  )
}

int_min <- slice_min(int_tests, p, n = 1)
tost_min_text <- h1b_tost |>
  mutate(txt = glue::glue(
    "{str_to_lower(measure)} ±{f2(min_bound)} points ({f2(min_bound_sd)} SD)"
  )) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  paste(collapse = ", ")
tost_quarter <- tost_grid |>
  filter(bound_label == "±0.25 points")
carry_prev <- carryover |>
  filter(term == "prev_not_asked")

dec_declined <- dec_contrasts |>
  filter(str_starts(contrast, "Declined"))
dec_mixed <- dec_contrasts |>
  filter(str_starts(contrast, "Mixed"))

rng <- \(x) paste0(f2(min(x)), "–", f2(max(x)))
abs_group <- filter(gap_group, str_starts(contrast, "\\|"))
abs_own <- filter(gap_own, str_starts(contrast, "\\|"))
own_cons <- filter(gap_own, contrast == "Consented gap")
own_decl <- filter(gap_own, contrast == "Declined gap")
own_signed <- filter(gap_own, str_detect(contrast, "signed"))

v_dc <- \(cmp) filter(own_v_dc, comparison == cmp)
sens <- \(f) filter(own_v_sens, fit == f)
n_declined_v <- own_gap_data |>
  filter(decision == "Declined both") |>
  count(vignette) |>
  pull(n)

h2_both <- h2 |> filter(model == "Both")
h2_text <- \(t) {
  r <- filter(h2_both, term == t)
  glue::glue("b = {f2(r$estimate)} [{f2(r$conf.low)}, {f2(r$conf.high)}], p {fp(r$p.value)}")
}
```

- **H1a (between-person, by vignette): not supported.** None of the 9
  Welch tests are significant (smallest unadjusted p = `r f2(h1a_min_p)`;
  smallest Holm-adjusted p = `r f2(min(h1a$p_holm))`), and the Wilcoxon
  tests agree. `r h1a_neg` of 9 differences are in the hypothesised direction;
  the V3 trust and acceptance differences point the other way. With about 29
  per group, these tests had 80% power only for differences of roughly
  d = `r f2(power_d)`, so moderate effects cannot be ruled out.
- **H1b (within-person): not supported.** Estimates are all slightly
  negative (Not asked lower) but small and not significant:
  `r h1b_text("Trust")`; `r h1b_text("Acceptance")`;
  `r h1b_text("Satisfaction")` (scale points, 95% CI, unadjusted p). The CIs
  rule out within-person drops larger than about
  `r f2(-min(h1b$conf.low))` points on any measure. The ordinal model for
  satisfaction gives the same conclusion.
- **H1b follow-ups.** The condition effect does not differ significantly
  across vignettes (strongest interaction: `r str_to_lower(int_min$measure)`,
  F(`r int_min$num_df`, `r round(int_min$den_df)`) = `r f2(int_min$F)`,
  p `r fp(int_min$p)`, Holm p `r fp(int_min$p_holm)`). Equivalence tests show
  the within-person effects are smaller than `r tost_min_text`; at a bound of
  ±0.25 points, equivalence holds for
  `r sum(tost_quarter$equivalent)` of 3 outcomes
  (`r paste(str_to_lower(tost_quarter$measure[tost_quarter$equivalent]), collapse = " and ")`).
  Whether this counts as negligible depends on the smallest effect of interest,
  which was not pre-specified. There is no evidence of carryover from the
  previous vignette's condition (p = `r f2(min(carry_prev$p.value))` to
  `r f2(max(carry_prev$p.value))`).
- **H2 (trust and acceptance predicting satisfaction): supported, mainly
  through acceptance.** In the joint model, within-person changes in both
  trust (`r h2_text("trust_w")`) and acceptance (`r h2_text("accept_w")`)
  predict satisfaction. Between people, acceptance predicts satisfaction
  (`r h2_text("accept_pm")`), but trust adds little once acceptance is
  accounted for (`r h2_text("trust_pm")`), although trust alone does predict
  it. The ordinal model agrees. These are same-time, same-source associations,
  not causal effects.
- **Exploratory: consent decision among Asked participants.** Ratings differ
  by decision for all three outcomes (largest Holm-adjusted p `r fp(max(dec_omnibus$p_holm))`).
  Compared with consenting to both requests, declining both is associated with
  ratings `r f2(min(-dec_declined$estimate))`–`r f2(max(-dec_declined$estimate))`
  points lower, and a mixed decision with ratings
  `r f2(min(-dec_mixed$estimate))`–`r f2(max(-dec_mixed$estimate))` points
  lower. The same participants also rate lower in vignettes where they were
  not asked (`r f2(min(disposition$estimate))`–`r f2(max(disposition$estimate))`
  points from accepting no requests to accepting all), so the decision largely
  marks participants' pre-existing stance towards MedHelper rather than an
  effect of consenting. The gap is somewhat larger in Asked than in Not asked
  vignettes for every outcome (difference
  `r f2(min(gap_interaction$estimate))`–`r f2(max(gap_interaction$estimate))`
  points), but none of these differences are significant (smallest Holm p
  `r fp(min(gap_interaction$p_holm))`) and the CIs run from about
  `r f2(min(gap_interaction$conf.low))` to `r f2(max(gap_interaction$conf.high))`,
  so an added effect of the decision can be neither confirmed nor ruled out.
- **Exploratory: is Not asked closer to consenters than to decliners?** At
  the group level, the Not asked–Declined gap exceeds the Not
  asked–Consented gap by `r rng(abs_group$estimate)` points, but not
  significantly after Holm correction (unadjusted p =
  `r f2(min(abs_group$p))`–`r f2(max(abs_group$p))`; Holm p ≥
  `r f2(min(abs_group$p_holm))`). Relative to each participant's own Not asked
  ratings, consenters rate `r rng(own_cons$estimate)` points higher and
  decliners `r rng(-own_decl$estimate)` points lower, so the two gaps are of
  similar size (absolute-gap difference `r rng(abs_own$estimate)`, all
  p ≥ `r f2(min(abs_own$p))`). The signed difference between them
  (`r rng(-own_signed$estimate)` points, Holm p ≤
  `r sprintf("%.3f", max(own_signed$p_holm))`) shows that ratings in the vignette where a
  participant declined are lower relative to their own baseline than ratings
  where they consented, which the person-level consent-rate analysis did not
  detect. This is still an association with a self-chosen decision, and it is
  fragile (next point).
- **Exploratory: is the own-baseline decline effect concentrated in V3?**
  There is no evidence that it differs by vignette (decision × vignette
  p = `r f2(min(own_v_int$p))`–`r f2(max(own_v_int$p))`, unadjusted). In V3,
  declined ratings are `r rng(-v_dc("V3")$estimate)` points lower than
  consented ratings (relative to own baseline), compared with
  `r rng(-v_dc("V1–V2 average")$estimate)` on average in V1–V2. But this test
  has almost no power (`r paste(n_declined_v, collapse = ", ")` "Declined
  both" ratings in V1–V3), and the significant result does lean on V3 and on
  a few people. Without the V3 "Declined both" ratings, the gap keeps its
  direction (`r rng(-sens("Without V3 Declined-both ratings")$estimate)`
  points lower) but is not significant for any outcome
  (p = `r f2(min(sens("Without V3 Declined-both ratings")$p))`–`r f2(max(sens("Without V3 Declined-both ratings")$p))`).
  Most of the evidence comes from the `r length(switchers)` participants whose
  decision differed between their two Asked vignettes. Without them, the gap
  shrinks to `r rng(-sens("Without decision switchers")$estimate)` points
  (all p ≥ `r f2(min(sens("Without decision switchers")$p))`). Of the
  `r sum(switcher_declines$participants)` switchers who declined both
  requests in one vignette, `r filter(switcher_declines, vignette == "V3")$participants`
  did so in V3. Weighting all observations equally (no random intercept)
  gives a gap of `r rng(-sens("No random intercept (CR1 SEs)")$estimate)`
  points, significant only for
  `r paste(str_to_lower(sens("No random intercept (CR1 SEs)")$measure[sens("No random intercept (CR1 SEs)")$p < .05]), collapse = " and ")`.
  The vignette-specific association is therefore weak evidence, resting
  mainly on a handful of participants who declined in V3.
